items.title: Start small to get something big
items.quote: There are a number of ways to manipulate you to do things that people want. I'm going to share three of them with you right now and then you can see if you can spot them in the future when somebody is trying to sell you something. Number one, they start small in order to get something big. Let's take the grocery store for instance. You get a taste of that little bread with some butter on, you say, tastes good and then you buy the whole loaf. Typical manipulation technique.

items.title: Start big to get something small
items.quote: The second one is the opposite. They start big in order to get something small. They ask for a lot and then when you say, oh, that's too much. Well, can you just give us that then? And then you will say, well, compared to the big ask, that's nothing. Of course I will. Then you give them something that you perhaps didn't even want to give in the first place. Very common technique.

items.title: Offer two options forcing choice
items.quote: And the third one is to just give you two options and none of them is about you saying no. It's about saying, do you want the red or the blue? Do you want it today or next week and so on. It's another manipulation technique that will make you decide upon those two instead of yes or no at all.

items.title: SITT SJÄLV
items.quote: 1. SITT SJÄLV. Alla ska vara uppkopplade på samma sätt. Mixen av att några sitter tillsammans och andra själva, ger ett sämre möte.

items.title: KOM I GOD TID
items.quote: 2. KOM I GOD TID. Som mötesledare är det bra om du är först in i telefon- konferensen. En mötesdeltagare behöver vara redo fem minuter innan ni drar igång. Allt för att minimera teknikstrul och för att hinna säga hej ordentligt.

items.title: TALA TYDLIGT
items.quote: 3. TALA TYDLIGT. Artikulera, betona och pausa för att få fram ditt budskap så bra som möjligt.

items.title: SAKTA NER
items.quote: 4. SAKTA NER. I ett telefonmöte kan du vinna på att dra ner tempot för att förstå bättre.

items.title: LYSSNA NOGA
items.quote: 5. LYSSNA NOGA. Du kan höra mycket om du bara lyssnar. Både känslor, tystnad och betoningar.

items.title: SKRIV NER VILKA SOM DELTAR
items.quote: 6. SKRIV NER VILKA SOM DELTAR. Så att du hela tiden vet vilka som talar och vilka som är tysta.

items.title: STÄNG AV LJUDET
items.quote: 7. STÄNG AV LJUDET när du inte pratar.

items.title: SÄG DITT NAMN
items.quote: 8. SÄG DITT NAMN innan du börjar så att alla vet vem som har ordet. Det är bra när ni är tre eller fler.

items.title: Ha en bra START- OCH STOPPRITUAL
items.quote: 9. Ha en bra START- OCH STOPPRITUAL. Som mötesledare kan du skapa goda förutsättningar genom att få igång alla i början på mötet och sedan av- sluta trevligt och utan stress. Bygg relationer, summera och kom överens om vem som gör vad. #virtuellamöten #ledarskap #kommunikation

items.title: MARTYERNA
items.quote: MARTYERNA tycker väldigt synd om sig själva. De alltid måste offra sig. De vill ge dig dåligt samvete, vare sig du är skyldig till detta elände eller inte. Samvetet är energivaluta som de snor av dig.

items.title: HEMLIGA
items.quote: De HEMLIGA vill att du ska undra varför de är så reserverade och varför du inte kan få dem att öppna sig mer. Det skapar en osäkerhet hos dig (en annan valuta), och du ger av din energi genom att ständigt fråga, men allt du får tillbaks är halva svar.

items.title: IFRÅGASÄTTARNA
items.quote: IFRÅGASÄTTARNA är ständigt kritiska. De kan säga ”Här var det stökigt”, ”Vad du ser sliten ut” eller ”Du borde ha mer ordning på dina fakta.” Sedan är energikampen igång. Om du inte har en stark självkänsla börjar du tvivla på dig själv och din energi byter ägare - från dig till dem.

items.title: HOTFULLA
items.quote: De HOTFULLA går ett steg längre. Med fysisk överlägsenhet, eller på andra hotfulla sätt sätter de skräck i dig. De är mobbarna i skolan som puttar och slåss. Det är de extremt osäkra vuxna som lärt sig att hot är enda sättet att få sin vilja igenom.

items.quote: Storytelling-SM för ett år sedan. Jag knep en hedrande bronsplats. I finalen var temat: "traditionsenligt" Jag valde en annorlunda tradition - en som många av er längtar efter nu när vi knappt får lämna hemmet. 5 minuter och bara storytelling. items.title: UPP MED NÄSAN
items.quote: 1. UPP MED NÄSAN. Skillnaden mellan att se arrogant ut och vanlig, är cirka en tum. Testa själv att höja näsan i luften cirka 2,54 cm. Nu ser du ner på din omgivning. Du upplevs arrogant.

items.title: TANKELÄS
items.quote: 2. TANKELÄS. Anta att du redan vet vad andra ska säga så slipper du lyssna klart och kan svara ändå, gärna genom att avbryta folk mitt i en mening. Om de alls får en syl i vädret förstås.

items.title: TA ÅT DIG ÄRAN
items.quote: 3. TA ÅT DIG ÄRAN. Låt inte någon annan skina, beröm så lite som möjligt och om någon i ditt team gjort något bra så ta åt dig äran själv. Det är ett bombsäkert sätt att skapa en arrogant identitet.

items.title: TITTA ÖVER AXELN
items.quote: 4. TITTA ÖVER AXELN på den du pratar med. Så att du signalerar att det kan dyka upp någon intressantare när som helst.

items.title: SÄG FEL NAMN
items.quote: 5. SÄG FEL NAMN. Och framför allt: Blir du rättad, vifta undan det som att det inte är viktigt. Fem tips. Fem sätt. Lycka till ^_^ #kommunikation #ledarskap #arbetsglädje #kundbemötande

items.title: IDENTITY goals
items.quote: 1. IDENTITY goals, i.e. WHO do you want to be? What's important for you? What purpose are you aiming to fulfill?

items.title: RESULT goals
items.quote: 2. RESULT goals i.e. WHAT turn-over, margins, market share, number of new customers, number of articles your are featured in etc. have you set up as an objective?

items.title: PERFORMANCE goals
items.quote: 3. PERFORMANCE goals i.e HOW will you get to the wanted results and the wanted identity? Identity goals are the most important ones. They are long lasting and determines your quality of life. Result goals can be motivating sometimes, and they are good for cost calculations, but they are outside of your control. Performance goals are within your control and adaptable. It's about taking those shots. Which ones do your company focus on? #leadership #engagement #goals

items.title: Get an external camera
items.quote: 1. Get an external camera. The one on the laptop is rarely good enough.

items.title: Use an external microphone
items.quote: 2. Use an external microphone. Preferably with "cardioid" function so that it directs its attention to your mouth and filters out the rest.

items.title: Have a light directed at you
items.quote: 3. Have a light directed at you. We want to see you clearly.

items.title: Use a neutral background
items.quote: 4. Use a neutral background. We don't want to see messy backgrounds any more.

items.title: Place the camera at eye level
items.quote: 5. Place the camera at eye level. No more nostrils and ceiling lights please.

items.title: Look into the camera while talking
items.quote: 6. Look into the camera while talking. Then it feels like we have eye contact.

items.title: Be yourself plus 10-20 percent
items.quote: 7. Be yourself plus 10-20 percent. You need to turn it up extra a notch when presenting online.

items.title: Stand up
items.quote: 8. Stand up. Then you get more energy which you can forward to the audience..

items.title: Keep your gestures closer to your head
items.quote: 9. Keep your gestures closer to your head. What we see of you is limited.

items.title: Mirror your gestures
items.quote: 10. Mirror your gestures. If you want to show that you go from A to B, do it from right to left. Then it will be right for the recipient. If you want more tips, I made a version with 33 tips for a customer recently. DM me.

items.title: JAG KAN TA DET PIANO NÄR ALLA ANDRA JOBBAR HÅRT
items.quote: 3. JAG KAN TA DET PIANO NÄR ALLA ANDRA JOBBAR HÅRT Säg att du drar i ett rep med en 100-kilostyngd i änden. Du orkar precis rubba tyngden. Om ni sedan är två lika starka personer borde ni kunna dra 200 kilo, eller? Fel. Ni klarar 180 kilo. Är ni sex personer kanske ni klarar 300 kilo. Det här kallas för Social loafing på psykologspråk. Vi får helt enkelt inte ut max av varje person när vi är ett lag. Det kan bero på flera anledningar. Någon maskar. Oklara mål och roller påverkar, och så vidare.

items.title: Keep the trigger and the reward but replace the behavior
items.quote: 1. Keep the trigger and the reward but replace the behavior. The program is hard coded so you can not delete it. But you can control your action. If the boss tells you to give a presentation and you want to feel useful; start by finding out the purpose, the objectives, the target audience and the key messages. Use pen and paper. Then practice how to present content without slides. When presenting: Notice how the participants are awake and alert.

items.title: Find your desire to change
items.quote: 2. Find your desire to change. You must really want something, for it to be worthwhile replacing the bad habit with a new better one. It requires effort, motivation, drive etc. Find your inspiration. Is it appreciation you are looking for? The power to influence? The pride in doing a good job? Find your reason, your purpose.

items.title: Believe that you can
items.quote: 3. Believe that you can. Believe it is achievable. If you fall you stand up again. Give yourself a pat on the back every time you succeed. Ask others to do it too and support you. items.title: Don’t use PowerPoint. Let yourself be the presentation.
items.quote: 1. Don’t use PowerPoint. Let yourself be the presentation. We actually survived hundreds of thousands of years before PowerPoint came along. Think about it.

items.title: The more information on the slides the less chance that the audience will remember anything.
items.quote: 2. The more information on the slides the less chance that the audience will remember anything.

items.title: If you show a slide – be quiet for a few seconds. Let the audience read it first. Remember: The audience cannot focus on you and the slides at the same time.
items.quote: 4. If you show a slide – be quiet for a few seconds. Let the audience read it first. Remember: The audience cannot focus on you and the slides at the same time.

items.quote: 8. Maximum number of font sizes: 3

items.quote: 9. The fewer bullet points the better. And: If you absolutely need an agenda slide – don’t write more than three bullets.

items.title: FORCE EVERYONE BACK INTO THE OFFICE FULL-TIME.
items.quote: 1. FORCE EVERYONE BACK INTO THE OFFICE FULL-TIME. Nobody wants to feel distrusted and such a decision makes employees feel forced into something they don't want. The feeling of micromanagement is present and the autonomy is gone. It's a motivational killer.

items.title: LEAVE EVERYTHING FREE TO EACH INDIVIDUAL TO DECIDE.
items.quote: 2. LEAVE EVERYTHING FREE TO EACH INDIVIDUAL TO DECIDE. It is equally wrong to abdicate one's leadership. It will create frustration, difficulties with cooperation, and misunderstandings. All this leads to lower engagement.

items.title: REDUCE THE NUMBER OF WORKPLACES.
items.quote: 3. REDUCE THE NUMBER OF WORKPLACES. Very few people like insecurity. By removing all fixed seats and also having fewer of them, you set the stage for more stress and frustration for those who come in later and find that they are "not wanted" and may not even have anywhere to sit.

items.title: CONTINUE WITH POWERPOINT CONFERENCES.
items.quote: 4. CONTINUE WITH POWERPOINT CONFERENCES. Not using the team's collective intelligence with the help of co-creation, discussions, and reflections was stupid before the pandemic. The difference is that people are now used to working digitally, so once you have a physical meeting, the demands are high for the physical meetings to be better. Otherwise, the result will be reduced engagement.

items.title: OFFER BUNS TO THOSE PHYSICALLY PRESENT AT MEETINGS.

tags.label: unequal benefits for remote vs office

items.quote: 5. OFFER BUNS TO THOSE PHYSICALLY PRESENT AT MEETINGS. A sure way to create an us-and-them feeling is for those in the office to receive benefits that the home workers cannot take part in. Those remote will feel like second-class employees and quickly lose motivation. What other good advice can you share, if you want a really bad hybrid workplace? #hybridleadership #communication #engagement this is an extract from a column I wrote for HR-nytt, a magazine for around 60,000 HR professionals. > hr

items.title: FORCE EVERYONE BACK INTO THE OFFICE FULL-TIME
items.quote: 1. FORCE EVERYONE BACK INTO THE OFFICE FULL-TIME. Nobody wants to feel distrusted and such a decision makes employees feel forced into something they don't want. The feeling of micromanagement is present and the autonomy is gone. It's a motivational killer.

items.title: LEAVE EVERYTHING FREE TO EACH INDIVIDUAL TO DECIDE
items.quote: 2. LEAVE EVERYTHING FREE TO EACH INDIVIDUAL TO DECIDE. It is equally wrong to abdicate one's leadership. It will create frustration, difficulties with cooperation, and misunderstandings. All this leads to lower engagement.

items.title: REDUCE THE NUMBER OF WORKPLACES
items.quote: 3. REDUCE THE NUMBER OF WORKPLACES. Very few people like insecurity. By removing all fixed seats and also having fewer of them, you set the stage for more stress and frustration for those who come in later and find that they are "not wanted" and may not even have anywhere to sit.

items.title: CONTINUE WITH POWERPOINT CONFERENCES
items.quote: 4. CONTINUE WITH POWERPOINT CONFERENCES. Not using the team's collective intelligence with the help of co-creation, discussions, and reflections was stupid before the pandemic. The difference is that people are now used to working digitally, so once you have a physical meeting, the demands are high for the physical meetings to be better. Otherwise, the result will be reduced engagement.

items.title: OFFER BUNS TO THOSE PHYSICALLY PRESENT AT MEETINGS
items.quote: 5. OFFER BUNS TO THOSE PHYSICALLY PRESENT AT MEETINGS. A sure way to create an us-and-them feeling is for those in the office to receive benefits that the home workers cannot take part in. Those remote will feel like second-class employees and quickly lose motivation. What other good advice can you share, if you want a really bad hybrid workplace? items.title: PREPARE.
items.quote: 1. PREPARE. - Have a clear goal and purpose for the workshop that you can explain. - Invite the right people. Include the goal and the purpose. This way, the participants' subconscious minds can get to work. - Create an agenda but fill it only to 80%, so you’ll have a margin if you need to adapt. - Create clear instructions for each step. In a workshop, the goal is set but the result is created by the group. It is your task to support that process. - Use larger rooms than normal meetings. Furnis

items.title: BE READY 5-10 MINUTES BEFORE YOU START
items.quote: 2. BE READY 5-10 MINUTES BEFORE YOU START - Make sure that everything works (pens, post-its, projector, whiteboard, flipchart, etc.) - Flip charts are great. Use them. - Greet the participants. Put on some music. - Group the participants with up to a maximum of 6 people around each table.

items.title: CREATE A POSITIVE ATMOSPHERE
items.quote: 3. CREATE A POSITIVE ATMOSPHERE · Start with an icebreaker. For example, you let the participants around each table share two truths and a lie about themselves. The others will guess which statement was a lie and which ones were true. Before a creative workshop, you can ask each group to come up with as many applications they can think of for an object like a book, toothpicks, a brick, etc. - Get them to share something that got them happy the last week or so. It also creates a nice buzz.

items.title: RUN THE WORKSHOP
items.quote: 4. RUN THE WORKSHOP - Use the IPA method for idea generation (first Individual, then Pair, then All.) That way, you get the introvert’s views because they will otherwise be shadowed by the extroverts. - Give attention to everyone. Encourage and praise the participants. Notice if someone is shying away or becoming disengaged. - Vary your methods so that it doesn’t become monotonous and tedious. - Signal control and comfort. That you are on top of things. They should not worry that the process doe

items.title: SUMMARIZE AND REFLECT
items.quote: 5. SUMMARIZE AND REFLECT - At the end of the workshop, you or the participants summarize what results/ideas/agreements, etc. the group has achieved. - If there are action points, highlight them a bit more. Who does what and when? - Reflect on the process: What was good about the workshop? What could be better? - Thank them all for investing their time, mind, and heart into the workshop. GOOD LUCK!

items.title: PRACTICE STANDING UP
items.quote: 1. PRACTICE STANDING UP. If you have a job at a desk, your feet are in for a shock if you don’t start standing at work, in the run-up to the show. Start a few weeks in advance. Stand and walk around more than you usually do.

items.title: TAKE A BREAK
items.quote: 2. TAKE A BREAK. Make sure to take a break every couple of hours. You need to rest both your legs and your head. The optimal setup would be to have an agreed schedule you can follow. If you don’t have one, it is, of course, important that you check in with your colleagues before leaving the booth.

items.title: RECHARGE your batteries during your breaks
items.quote: 3. RECHARGE your batteries during your breaks. Do not wander around the trade show, visiting other booths. Leave the exhibition hall and recharge with what you need at the time: food, drink, a comfortable chair, fresh air...

items.title: WERE COMFORTABLE SHOES
items.quote: 4. WERE COMFORTABLE SHOES. After a few hours, a pair of shoes can pinch. A new pair to change into could be a good idea. Make sure to break in new shoes before the exhibition.

items.title: CHANGE SOCKS
items.quote: 5. CHANGE SOCKS. We sweat approximately 4 cl a day per foot. If you change socks it will feel better. There are also compression socks that help with blood circulation.

items.title: BREATH – the right way
items.quote: 6. BREATH – the right way. In pressured situations, our breathing accelerates and we do not fill our lungs to their maximum capacity. That makes us even more stressed out. Breathe slower to feel better.

items.title: TAKE CARE OF YOUR VOICE
items.quote: 7. TAKE CARE OF YOUR VOICE. Try to lower your pitch, and talk with the support of your stomach, instead of pressing your vocal cords. That way you will not strain your system so badly and you will have a deeper and more confidence-inspiring voice.

items.title: DRINK WATER
items.quote: 8. DRINK WATER Even if the room is cool and you don’t sweat a lot, the air is usually very dry in the big, air-conditioned halls. Get in the habit of taking a sip of water between conversations. Your breath will also stay fresher and it will help your vocal cords.

items.title: WATCH WHAT YOU EAT
items.quote: 9. WATCH WHAT YOU EAT. Remember that a shift in a booth is as tough as any other physical workout. You need to stock up on energy. Remember to eat a proper breakfast - things that are filling, but not indigestible. Eat fruit and snacks occasionally, but avoid sweets that get your blood sugar levels going.

items.title: HOLD BACK ON ALCOHOL the night before
items.quote: 10. HOLD BACK ON ALCOHOL the night before. Do not party hard at night. Think of it as competing in sports the day after. How would you prepare yourself then?

items.title: HAVE FUN
items.quote: 11. HAVE FUN. Be in a good mood. Give each other a high five, hand out compliments, laugh, and feel good. Later this year, publishing firm Austin Macauley will release my book Speed Selling, a book for those of you who want to generate high-quality leads in a booth. These tips will be included ^_^ #tradeshow #communication #speedselling

items.title: Lead by Example
items.quote: 1. Lead by Example: As leaders, we are the cultural compass of our organizations. By embodying the values we hold dear in our actions and decisions, we inspire others to do the same. Consistency from the top fosters a sense of unity that transcends physical spaces. One way is to watch out for Proximity bias, meaning that you promote the people sitting physically close to you.

items.title: Embrace Virtual Bonding
items.quote: 2. Embrace Virtual Bonding: Physical distance need not translate to emotional detachment. Embrace virtual team-building initiatives, workshops, and social events. These interactions build camaraderie and help employees remain connected to the shared culture. We did that a lot at the beginning of the pandemic, but nowadays, I see less of it.

items.title: Amplify Communication
items.quote: 3. Amplify Communication: Regularly communicate the organization's mission, vision, and values. Keep these messages alive through various channels, ensuring that your team remains aligned with the company's larger purpose. This is so easy to forget in everyday activities and to-do lists.

items.title: Champion Personal Stories
items.quote: 4. Champion Personal Stories: Encourage employees to share personal stories that showcase how they embody the company's values in their remote work setups. These anecdotes humanize the organization and strengthen the sense of belonging. We are not only functions. We are persons.

items.title: Consistent Branding
items.quote: 5. Consistent Branding: Consistency is key. Maintain a uniform brand across all communications, irrespective of work location. A cohesive brand presence reinforces the company's identity and cultivates a shared sense of pride. Or as one of my clients said: "It's about how you show up" Remember, flexible work arrangements can enhance your organization's dynamism and global reach. items.title: Always think digital first
items.quote: 1. Always think digital first. As soon as you have some remote, it is the digital channels that rule. Let everyone work in Zoom, preferably by using their own laptop. No more meetings where the remote participants are second-class colleagues. Start from them instead. Then you meet on equal terms. Hybrid IS digital first and foremost

items.title: Involve everyone and decide what is the right behavior and the right treatment
items.quote: 2. Involve everyone and decide what is the right behavior and the right treatment. If you are best at hybrid meetings; how are you then? Who does what? How do you treat each other? Which channels do you use? What is ok to do and what is not ok? Here, a workshop is smart to put in so that you agree on how you will meet.

items.title: Work with the WE feeling and skip the buns and cookies on site
items.quote: 3. Work with the WE feeling and skip the buns and cookies on site. Remote participants will not be motivated by seeing you sitting around a conference table with cinnamon buns and chai lattes. It just creates a feeling of injustice and that the people in the office are the A-team while the rest are the B-team. You hardly want it that way.

items.title: Have physical meetings, at least sometimes
items.quote: 4. Have physical meetings, at least sometimes. Analog is still by far the richest experience for participants. It is easier to build relationships, sense moods and address complex issues. If you have a distributed team where people sit far away, get together regularly from time to time, maybe off-site, and socialize. If everyone lives close by, you can do it more often. You have the opportunity to get the best of both worlds - analog and digital - if you do it right. Thanks for reading my mind /

items.title: Look at those in front of you
items.quote: 1. Look at those in front of you. Do not look at the floor, ceiling, walls, or out the window for more than a short time. You don't want to break the connection.

items.title: Hold your gaze for three seconds
items.quote: 2. Hold your gaze for three seconds. Anything less makes you seem insecure. More makes you seem combative. Or flirtatious. Switch to a new person, preferably in a zig-zag fashion.

items.title: Look at one part/group at a time
items.quote: 3. If you have a large audience, look at one part/group at a time. Everyone in that group thinks you looking at them. When you talk to fewer people:

items.title: Look away occasionally when you speak
items.quote: 4. Look away occasionally when you speak. Feel free to reinforce with nods to show that you are actively listening and present.

items.title: Look at the other person to invite them to speak
items.quote: 5. When you want the other person to speak, you look at him/her. As an invite saying it is their turn. So there. Good luck with the eye contact! ​ #keynotespeaker #communicationcoach #leadership #communication #engagement

items.title: Be clear
items.quote: 1. Be clear. Unclear goals, unclear roles, and unclear responsibilities are motivational killers.

items.title: Show trust
items.quote: 2. Show trust. The more autonomy, the greater the motivation.

items.title: Visualize together
items.quote: 3. Visualize together. Paint a picture of how good it will be when it's done.

items.title: Clear out obstacles
items.quote: 4. Clear out obstacles. If a department is a bottleneck, work on a solution.

items.quote: 5. Celebrate successes. We all want to be validated and appreciated. Motivation comes from the Latin word movere; to move. People want to perform, people want to move towards a goal. Help them do it. Feel the joy when it happens. PS - How do you stay motivated?

items.title: Focus on Value, Not Features
items.quote: 1. 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗩𝗮𝗹𝘂𝗲, 𝗡𝗼𝘁 𝗙𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 Talk value and people will be interested. Talk features, and most people switch off or get confused. Your choice.

items.title: Understand the Customer's Perspective
items.quote: 2. 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿'𝘀 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 Find out what is important to the customer and why. Then focus on explaining the value of your solution according to what the customer has told you.

items.title: Be an Active Listener
items.quote: 3. 𝗕𝗲 𝗮𝗻 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗿 Listen actively by showing genuine interest, nodding, and summarizing the customer’s points to confirm understanding.

items.title: Build Empathy
items.quote: 4. 𝗕𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱 𝗘𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗵𝘆 Tip: Empathy in sales builds stronger connections. Understand your customer's perspective to tailor your solutions effectively.

items.title: Handle Objections with Grace
items.quote: 5. 𝗛𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗹𝗲 𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗚𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗲 Prepare and handle objections gracefully to turn potential "no" into a "yes."

items.title: Use Storytelling
items.quote: 6. 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗦𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘆𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 Use compelling stories to highlight the benefits of your product and connect emotionally with your customers.

items.title: Recognize Buying Signals
items.quote: 7. 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗴𝗻𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗕𝘂𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗦𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘀 Recognize buying signals to close the deal. Look for engagement cues and specific product questions.

items.title: Practice Active Listening
items.quote: 8. 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗔𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 Show that you are listening by nodding, maintaining eye contact, and responding appropriately. Reflect back on what you've heard to confirm your understanding.

items.title: Personalize Your Approach
items.quote: 9. 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗮𝗰𝗵 Tailor your sales pitch to meet the specific needs and preferences of each customer. Use their name, mention their company, and address their unique challenges.

items.title: Follow Up Promptly
items.quote: 10. 𝗙𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗼𝘄 𝗨𝗽 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘁𝗹𝘆 Always follow up after a meeting or a call. Send a thank-you email summarizing key points discussed and the next steps. This shows your commitment and keeps the conversation going.

items.title: Utilize Social Proof

items.title: Acknowledgement sets you apart
items.quote: 𝟭. 𝗔𝗰𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗮𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁. The bar for service is very low. Seeing people, greeting them, and acknowledging them puts you ahead of most.

items.title: Internal culture becomes customer experience
items.quote: 𝟮. 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗯𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲. How people meet, greet, and treat each other directly affects how customers are treated.

items.title: Empowerment beats manuals
items.quote: 𝟯. 𝗘𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗯𝗲𝗮𝘁𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘂𝗮𝗹𝘀. Memorable service comes from people who feel trusted to act, not from scripts and policies.

items.title: One company can have several cultures at once
items.quote: 𝟰. 𝗢𝗻𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘆 𝗰𝗮𝗻 𝗵𝗮𝘃𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝘁 𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗲. Customers notice when departments operate with different attitudes. The organization must “sing the same song.”

items.title: Mindset drives communication, which drives engagement
items.quote: 𝟱. 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗱𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻, 𝘄𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗵 𝗱𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝗲𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁. The chain is: 𝗠𝗶𝗻𝗱𝘀𝗲𝘁 → 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 → 𝗘𝗻𝗴𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 → 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 → 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁 → 𝗦𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵 Fear can drive performance short term. This chain drives it long-term.

items.title: Positivity powers performance
items.quote: 𝟲. 𝗣𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲. High-performing teams have far more positive interactions than average teams. A positive mood measurably improves effectiveness.

items.title: Emotional contagion is real
items.quote: 𝟳. 𝗘𝗺𝗼𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗶𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗹. Mood spreads. People carry your energy to others. The key question: 𝗔𝗿𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝗽𝗽𝗶𝗲𝗿 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗼𝗼𝗺, 𝗼𝗿 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗹𝗲𝗮𝘃𝗲?

items.title: The three communication superpowers
items.quote: 𝟴. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘀𝘂𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿𝘀 • 𝗘𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗴𝘆 – People believe that you believe (non-verbal impact) • 𝗘𝗺𝗽𝗮𝘁𝗵𝘆 – People feel understood (listen to understand) • 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 – People understand and remember (simplicity beats complexity) Empathy is the foundation. If you don’t understand others, you cannot make yourself understood.

items.title: Clarity is subtraction
items.quote: 𝟵. 𝗖𝗹𝗮𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝘀𝘂𝗯𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻. People cannot act on what they don’t remember. Stories, metaphors, and the power of three make messages stick. Remove clutter in slides, emails, and language. Would you value a summary like this after a speech? What are your thoughts?

items.quote: Empathy creates engagement. Engagement leads to behavior. Behavior leads to results.

items.title: Find out if this is a debate or a discussion
items.quote: 1. Find out if this is a 𝗱𝗲𝗯𝗮𝘁𝗲 or a 𝗱𝗶𝘀𝗰𝘂𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻. Debate is about winning or losing. A discussion has no winner. Instead, everyone contributes and listens.

items.title: Ask yourself two questions before you join the panel
items.quote: 2. Ask yourself two questions before you join the panel: • What do you want the audience to 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄, 𝗳𝗲𝗲𝗹, and 𝗱𝗼 with what you say? • What would you like to 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄 from the 𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲? It is almost always possible to get at least a hand raised to create engagement.

items.title: Talk to the moderator in advance
items.quote: 3. Talk to the 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿 in advance so that he/she know what you want, where you stand, and what questions could be appropriate.

items.title: Look at the person speaking
items.quote: 𝟰. 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗸 𝗮𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴. If you look in a different direction, the audience will not know what to focus on. If you look at the speaker, the audience will do the same.

items.title: When answering the moderator
items.quote: 5. When answering the moderator: 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗸 at the 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗼𝗿 first, then go out to the 𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 and to your fellow 𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗲𝗹 𝗺𝗲𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗿𝘀, and when you're finished, return to the moderator. It will be great!

items.title: Associate, reflect, join
items.quote: 6. Associate, reflect, join. 𝗕𝗲 𝗮𝗰𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲. It will be much more engaging for the audience if the moderator doesn't have to fight for each answer.

items.title: Prepare some great one‑liners and metaphors in advance

items.title: Understand the purpose of the event
items.quote: 𝟭. 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝘂𝗿𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘁 Why does the event exist? What is it meant to achieve? What kind of atmosphere does the client want to create? How can you contribute to that?

items.title: Understand the speakers’ target audiences
items.quote: 𝟮. 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀’ 𝘁𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲𝘀 Find out whether the speakers share the same audience or have different ones. You need to understand which audience each speaker wants to reach. Your role is to represent the audience while also helping the speaker shine.

items.title: Understand each speaker’s goal with their presentation
items.quote: 𝟯. 𝗨𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀𝘁𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿’𝘀 𝗴𝗼𝗮𝗹 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗶𝗿 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 What do they want the audience to know? What do they want the audience to feel? What do they want the audience to do?

items.title: Review the speakers’ material in advance
items.quote: 𝟰. 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀’ 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗶𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲 This allows you to identify interesting questions you can ask the speaker before or after their presentation.

items.title: Ask the speakers how they want to be introduced
items.quote: 𝟱. 𝗔𝘀𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗵𝗼𝘄 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘄𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗯𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗲𝗱 Build their credibility. Set the right tone. If the client wants an informal atmosphere, you can, for example, include something personal in the introduction. Also, do your own research.

items.title: Ask the speakers which questions they would like you to ask
items.quote: 𝟲. 𝗔𝘀𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝘄𝗵𝗶𝗰𝗵 𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝘆 𝘄𝗼𝘂𝗹𝗱 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝘁𝗼 𝗮𝘀𝗸 What does the speaker believe the audience wants to know more about? Dare to ask the “stupid questions.” The audience will thank you. When the audience is large, I advise skipping open Q&A sessions. Otherwise, there is a risk that a know-it-all will step in and ruin the atmosphere you and the speaker have built. On the other hand, if you have a positive atmosphere filled with trust; go for it!

items.title: Link one presentation to the next – convey the common thread
items.quote: 𝟳. 𝗟𝗶𝗻𝗸 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝗲𝘅𝘁 – 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗱 The audience should feel completely safe with you as a moderator and sense that there is a clear reason for both the topics and the order in which they are presented.

items.title: You are running a marathon, not a 100‑meter sprint
items.quote: 𝟴. 𝗬𝗼𝘂 𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝗿𝘂𝗻𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗵𝗼𝗻, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮 𝟭𝟬𝟬-𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗻𝘁 The 100 meters are for the speakers. You will be on stage many times, so you need to manage your energy. Instead of giving 100%, 85% is enough — with full engagement, of course.

items.title: End on a positive note
items.quote: 𝟵. 𝗘𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝗻 𝗮 𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗻𝗼𝘁𝗲 Always end the parts you moderate in a major key, not a minor one. Do not let anyone finish with a negative comment before the speaker or the entire event concludes. That is what the audience will remember. Make sure they leave with a good aftertaste. There you go. If you wanna dig deeper, I wrote a book about it, called Moderate great 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝘆 𝗴𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁 ^_^

items.title: Jobba inkluderande på möten
items.quote: # 2 Jobba inkluderande på möten Digitala möten behöver innehålla en balans mellan det professionella och det privata. Detta är på plats för att alla ska känna sig delaktiga. Det går att göra genom att ställa öppna frågor till alla. Det är också viktigt att alla får en och samma ingång i mötena. ”Du ska inte ha olika skärmar i förhållande till varandra”, säger Lacinai.

items.title: Lägg krut på teamkänsla
items.quote: # 3 Lägg krut på teamkänsla Det finns en ökande efterfrågan att arbeta på distans. Ett problem med detta är att teamkänslan kan bli lidande. Det leder till att ”du får inte höra så många samtal som rör den mjuka sidan av medarbetarna”. Du som chef kan motverka detta genom att anordna en teambuilding en gång i månaden. Det kan också hjälpa till att ha en chattkanal för att ”alla ska känna sig sedda”.

items.title: Odla ett starkt självledarskap
items.quote: # 4 Odla ett starkt självledarskap Fokus på ledarskap har gått från det hierarkiska till det självledande. Lacinai menar att ”självledarskap är grunden för allt gott”. Detta beror på att det är ”viktigt att du som medarbetare också är med på den digitala resan, du är dina beslut från ditt hemma-kontor”. Det handlar om att du som medarbetare ”är närvarande och visar engagemang”.

items.title: Vässa möten och följ upp ofta
items.quote: # 5 Vässa möten och följ upp ofta En annan förändring med fokus på teamledarskap är att ”du behöver vässa dina möten”. Det kommer att kräva att du som chef planerar dina möten extra noga för att ”alla ska kunna vara med på tåget och känna sig hörda”. Följ också upp dina möten genom att skicka mejl till deltagarna med en sammanfattning. Det gör att ”alla vet vad som kommer att hända”.
